question: to the Commission Jorge Buxadé Villalba (PfE) Subject:

On 28 August 2026, the residents of Ceuta protested against the Moroccan Government’s invasion of the city through the coordinated influx of tens of thousands of Maghrebi people. During the protests, some of the illegal immigrants threw chemical devices/explosive weapons at the Ceutan residents who were defending their right to live in safety. According to media reports1, the weapons were made by NGO No Name Kitchen, an organisation seeking to destroy ‘Europe’s racist and violent borders’, and distributed to illegal immigrants to use against EU citizens. Although No Name Kitchen criticises the EU and states that it does not receive funds from the bloc, there are reports linking the organisation with Open Society Foundations2, an entity that does receive EU funding. In view of the above: 1.
Can the Commission confirm that No Name Kitchen has never received EU funding?
Does the Commission consider it appropriate to withdraw EU funding from Open Society Foundations since it is associated with radical groups that facilitate and encourage violence against Europeans?

Does the Commission consider that, in light of the evidence that No Name Kitchen is involved in organised criminal activities, it should support No Name Kitchen’s inclusion in Europol’s and INTERPOL’s criminal network databases?
